subject: Post-demo recap: procurement route (Marketplace vs PO) + next steps - Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@nimbus.ai>, Tyler Nguyen <tyler@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: procurement route (Marketplace vs PO) + next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really enjoyed the conversation and getting a clearer picture of Nimbus Analytics' latency and cost goals for inference. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement can evaluate paths in parallel: 

Highlights from the call:
- Target production start: mid-Q3 (approx. July).
- Expected steady-state usage: ~8–12M tokens / month (spikes higher during batch runs).
- Priority: predictable unit costs and ability to enforce VPC/private deployment for PHI processing.

Procurement path options we discussed:
1) Direct invoiced PO (Redwood contract + standard MSAs) — preferred if Nimbus requires longer invoicing terms and needs a purchase order flow.
2) Cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) — faster procurement for some teams; easier for single-click procurement but seller fees and Marketplace uplift can change unit economics.
3) Card/self-serve — possible for pilot accounts but unlikely for production.

Action items I need from Nimbus to finalize a proposal:
- Confirm procurement contact (I’ve copied procurement@nimbus.ai; please confirm this is the right inbox).
- Confirm preferred purchase route (AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace, direct PO, or card).
- Estimated committed monthly spend (even a range helps).
- Any required procurement docs aside from the usual (W-9, SOC2): specific contract terms, PO templates, or NDA redlines.

Attachments: preliminary pricing summary and SOC2 summary attached for procurement review.

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll produce a formal one-page commercial proposal + purchase options and send to procurement@nimbus.ai by EOD tomorrow.
- Offer sandbox access for a limited test cluster (if you want, I can spin up a 48-hour sandbox for your infra team).
- Follow-up call to align legal/finance: propose Tue Apr 5, 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.inference
[Attachment: redwood-proposal-nimbus-2027Q3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@nimbus.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Tyler Nguyen <tyler@nimbus.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement route (Marketplace vs PO) + next steps

Camila — thanks for the clear recap and the materials. A few items from procurement/cloud ops side: 

1) Procurement contact: procurement@nimbus.ai is correct for legal/invoice routing. Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need the following: W-9, SOC 2 summary, standard vendor questionnaire answers, and a sample PO-friendly invoice.

2) Preferred path: we prefer to purchase via PO (standard 30-day net terms) for production. That said, we're evaluating AWS Marketplace for speed of procurement for the initial pilot — will need to see pricing delta and whether any marketplace uplift is absorbed or passed through.

3) Commit estimate: likely to start ~6–8M tokens/mo for pilot, ramping to 10–12M tokens/mo in 60–90 days.

4) Timeline: procurement lead will need a one-page quote and the Redwood standard PO/contract sample. Typical procurement turnaround is 2–4 weeks once we have the final proposal and W-9/contract.

Could you include a direct comparison of expected monthly invoice under: (A) Redwood direct PO pricing vs (B) AWS Marketplace listing (including marketplace fee and any change to billing cadence)? If you can also note any discounts or onboarding credits available if we commit 12 months that would be helpful.

Thanks — Asha

—
Asha Patel
Head of Cloud Ops
Nimbus Analytics
asha.patel@nimbus.ai

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement route (Marketplace vs PO) + next steps

Thanks Asha — great context. I’ve attached a short cost comparison (marketplace-vs-direct-cost-breakdown.csv) that shows expected billed amount under a) direct PO with Redwood list pricing and b) AWS Marketplace purchase (includes typical AWS marketplace fee pass-through). High-level notes: 

- Marketplace typically increases list-unit price by ~8–12% due to marketplace transaction fees and reseller margins. Exact delta depends on channel (AWS vs GCP).
- Redwood can support both purchase flows: direct PO (monthly invoicing, net-30) or AWS Marketplace (monthly bill via AWS).
- For a 12-month committed term we can offer a one-time onboarding credit — details below.

Proposed next steps: 
- I’ll send a formal one-page proposal (Proforma) to procurement@nimbus.ai by EOD today with both purchase options clearly called out.
- If you want marketplace pricing highlighted, tell me whether AWS or GCP is preferred; I’ll show both side-by-side.
- Sandbox: I can enable a 48-hour private sandbox for Tyler and your infra team once procurement signals pilot approval.

On discounts: CC’ing Karthik (VP, Sales) to confirm — we typically offer a one-time onboarding credit for first-year commitments. Karthik, can you confirm rough credit range for a 12-month commit at the expected volumes?

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: marketplace-vs-direct-cost-breakdown.csv (CSV)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement route (Marketplace vs PO) + next steps

Quick note — can confirm we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the estimated first-year committed spend if Nimbus signs a 12-month commit and agrees to list purchase via AWS Marketplace OR direct PO. The credit is limited to the first invoice cycle (applied as a credit memo).

Camila: if you outline the expected annualized spend (use the mid-point of 10M tokens/mo) I’ll sign off the credit and legal can prepare a short amendment.

Karthik
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
